artifact.name: 19-audit-conflicts
artifact.purpose: Cross-artifact semantic deduplication and conflict analysis for type identities, layouts, vtables, inheritance, lifecycle, and naming evidence.
artifact.scope: Read-only analysis of the JSON partitions in knowledgegraph/research/types. No worker, source, SPORE, Ghidra, knowledge-graph, or history file is modified.

method.identity_rule: A proposed canonical ID is an indexing key, not a silent semantic resolution. Names are merged only when a stable binary association, matching layout, or independently corroborated structural contract supports the relation. Otherwise alternatives remain separate.
method.canonical_id_rule: Use lowercase namespace, kind, and normalized name, for example sim.cell-game-state, app.igame-mode, or unknown.vtable.013f1a30. Anonymous candidates use stable address or stable candidate ID instead of invented class names.

source_precedence.use: Observed bytes, exact addresses, and positive runtime traces.
source_precedence.limit: No positive original-game trace is present in these partitions.

source_precedence.use: Persisted raw structure, field, function, and disassembly exports.
source_precedence.limit: Exports can contain imported names, decompiler typing, and incomplete boundaries.

source_precedence.use: Direct decompilation operations, exact field accesses, and bounded lifecycle observations.
source_precedence.limit: Decompiler names, register types, and indirect calls remain bounded.

source_precedence.use: Community SDK names, declared sizes, field offsets, interfaces, and vtable slots.
source_precedence.limit: Reference-only provenance; declarations are not original behavior or RTTI.

source_precedence.use: Structural candidate boundaries, call/data references, labels, and category projections.
source_precedence.limit: A vtable candidate or reference is not class identity, ownership, or runtime reachability.

source_precedence.use: Campaign, atlas, dossier, and reconstruction assessments.
source_precedence.limit: Secondary claims may preserve stale, phase-specific, or conflicting source records.
Current source cannot establish original ABI, runtime semantics, or ownership.

merge_precedence.rule: Exact pinned binary/runtime observation wins for identity and observed behavior.
merge_precedence.application: Use only when a direct observation is explicitly present; do not infer one from a type name.

merge_precedence.rule: Direct field/offset/body evidence wins over a name-only SDK or current-source interpretation.
merge_precedence.application: Preserve the conflicting field meaning or ABI when a direct body disagrees.

merge_precedence.rule: Independent matching size, field-prefix, and consumer evidence supports an alias cluster.
merge_precedence.application: Canonicalize names within the cluster but keep unresolved subtype, vtable, and semantic claims separate.

merge_precedence.rule: SDK declarations establish reference names, declared layouts, and slot contracts only.
merge_precedence.application: Never use SDK inheritance or a slot name to erase a binary/body conflict.

merge_precedence.rule: Vtable/xref/triage evidence supports structural candidates and connectivity only.
merge_precedence.application: Keep the candidate under an address-based ID until a constructor, body, or independent class evidence resolves it.

merge_precedence.rule: Current source and historical synthesis are comparison/context evidence.
merge_precedence.application: Use them to identify limits and alternatives, not to promote clean-room approximations to original identity.

dimension_rules: Names and identity are dimensioned separately from layout.
A matching field prefix is a layout relationship, not proof of C++ inheritance when MSVC RTTI is absent.
A vtable size is not necessarily a class size; a candidate pointer run is not necessarily a complete table.
A vtable-reference edge identifies the containing base, not an exact selected slot.
A current-source field, pool, event, or interface can be a projection or replacement boundary rather than the original entity.
Null, unknown, and not-applicable values are retained rather than converted to zero or an inferred value.

SporeApp.exe has no MSVC RTTI; vtable candidates, shared prefixes, and SDK names do not establish unique C++ class identity or language-level inheritance.
The exact SDK identities and universal semantics of cObjectPool_ Initialize, CreateObject, Get, and DeleteObject remain unresolved around the address/body conflicts.
The relationship between 0x00E82340, 0x00E82420, and cCellDataReference_::Create is unresolved.
cGameData::Write at 0x00B184C0 has teardown-like body mechanics and remains a contested function identity.
EditorModel, cGameInputManager, 0x01490BE8, the UTFWin 21-slot bases, and other high-value candidates do not have one proven vtable base.
ITerrain 74 versus 75 slots, UTFWin candidate 40-slot runs, and IGameMode 16 versus cCellModeStrategy 27 remain dimension-specific alternatives.
cCreatureGameData 0x4C versus 0x50 and cSpeciesProfile 0xEEC versus 0xA18 are not resolved by the supplied evidence.
cPlanetRecord civ/tribe offsets and cStarManager selected field offsets have two preserved source layouts.
The cSpaceInventoryItem/cSpaceToolData shared inventory prefix has incompatible field-offset maps across 05-empire-space.json and 12-field-archaeology.json.
The 0x14-byte registration Entry and 0x18-byte ProcessQueue record are distinct; queue ownership, priority direction, send/post timing, and removal semantics remain unresolved.
FUN_00B21340 cannot be assigned to App message registration or noun/map materialization without stronger direct owner evidence.
cEditorAnimEvent, AnimationMessage, IAnimWorld, and renderer/pose ownership have no complete event-to-pose trace.
PROP, SPO, serializer stream framing, ClassSerializer bodies, object-pointer encoding, version migration, and round-trip order remain unresolved.
The anonymous 27-field and 24-field space records lack exact SDK layout, size, owner, consumer ordering, and serialization evidence.
Star/planet generation formulas, empire economy mutation, mission transitions, trade formulas, palette initialization, and global ownership remain unresolved.
Unnamed simulator accessors in the 0x00B3D220-0x00B3D5A0 region cannot be assigned to concrete owners/types from adjacency or fan-in alone.
The pdtk text command grammar, toolkit ownership, and response protocol remain unresolved; observed commands are a protocol channel, not a portable C++ type.
Global shutdown order across mode, CellGame, CellGFX, CellUI, message, resource, editor, and manager services is not recovered.
Current OpenSpore layouts, vectors, event records, resource providers, and mode shells are comparison surfaces and cannot backfill original ABI, ownership, or runtime semantics.

determinism.json_format: UTF-8 JSON object with stable key order and two-space indentation
determinism.array_order: ID-indexed conflict, duplicate, source-reference, and alternative arrays are sorted lexicographically by their stable keys; the entity catalog uses a stable namespace/category order.
determinism.identity_order: Canonical entity IDs are stable and unique; the catalog is emitted in a deterministic namespace/category order, while conflicts are grouped by category and sorted by conflict_id.
determinism.resolution_order: Alternatives are retained before disposition; no array ordering implies semantic precedence unless the merge_precedence field states it.
